title: [Decision] Formula inspector: prove a quantity read through a relationship, or keep the declared currency as an accepted limit (hop arm of #35815)
body:
repo:objectstack#8 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcSAaBEfQpU2yJexSJ8

Filing gate ②, Source: fleet. Carries the relationship-hop arm of #35815; #35815 keeps the field-over-field arm and rider N3 (PR #38108).

## 维护者速读

- 问题:作者在 Studio 里把一个"金额"公式改成"经关联对象读到的数量"(例如客户的员工数乘以二)后,这个字段仍带着货币符号显示;只影响显示,存的数不变。自带示例和平台对象里今天没有一条公式是这种写法。
- 选项:A 维持现状,作者手动把结果类型改回数字,不需要新 PR;B 让系统读取关联对象的字段后自动撤掉货币标记,约两个 PR,并且要扩大一个已对外发布的接口。
- 推荐 A:没有人撞上这个写法,而 B 要为这一种写法永久多维护一段对外接口。
- 不定会怎样:现状就是 A 的效果,已合入修复的"本对象字段相乘/相除"不受影响;只是这一支一直挂着没有结论。

## Background

After #35631 (PR #35774) Studio's formula inspector withdraws a declared `currency` only when `inferFormulaReturn` answers `number` ("proved not money"). PR #38108 makes it answer `number` for field-over-field quantity arithmetic and same-currency ratios. One shape #35815 named is left: a quantity read through a lookup or master-detail hop, `record.account.employee_count * 2`. The function is handed the host object's field map only, so the leaf's unit cannot be read; it answers `{}` and the declared `currency` stays. PR #38108 records this in the producer header as an accepted limit and reports it as a decision.

One-sentence question: an author who rewrites a money formula into a number read from a related record still sees a currency symbol on that field until they change the result type by hand; should the platform prove that case or leave it to the author?

Governing text: `packages/spec/src/data/field.zod.ts:2731-2746` on origin/main `93fa9118`: "Authoring stamps it from the inferred CEL type; absent when the type can't be proven (an ambiguous/`dyn` expression), except that a declared `percent` or `currency` stays", and authoring "withdraws a declared `currency` … when an edit leaves it answering `number`". `packages/formula/src/formula-return.ts:99-103`: "`returnType` — absent means NO verdict, never \"declares nothing\": the expression proves no type (`{}`, unproven), and a stamp keeps what the author declared (a `currency`, a `percent`). `number` means proved not money." Same file `:64-65` lists the hop among the unproven reads: "a hop through a reference (`record.account.balance`) — the leaf's type is not on this object". ADR: none found (`git grep -nE "inferFormulaReturn" origin/main -- docs/adr` → 0 lines; `git grep -ciE "returnType" origin/main -- docs/adr` → one file, ADR-0079, unrelated).

Protocol: neither option conflicts with the governing text. A changes nothing. B changes no `packages/spec` schema and no metadata key, but widens the published `@objectstack/formula` surface (`inferFormulaReturn` input or `FormulaSourceField`): Clause-②: yes (widening), Metadata-protocol: none.

## Premises (each with its re-check)

1. The hop answers `{}` on the PR head. `git grep -n "employee_count" b9bc5f06 -- packages/formula/src/formula-return.test.ts` → line 279 pins `toEqual({})`.
2. Zero first-party pull. `git grep -nE "returnType:\s*['\"]currency['\"]" origin/main -- examples packages/platform-objects skills | grep -vE "CHANGELOG|\.test\."` → 2 declarations (`examples/app-crm/src/objects/opportunity.object.ts:81`, `examples/app-showcase/src/data/objects/project.object.ts:99`); both read only same-object fields. Control (the population is reachable): hop reads in first-party formulas, ``git grep -nE "(cel|F)\`[^\`]*record\.[a-z_0-9]+\.[a-z_]+[^(a-z_]" origin/main -- examples packages/platform-objects skills | grep -vE "CHANGELOG|\.test\."`` → 6 lines, all `returnType: 'text'` display-name formulas in `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/`. Numeric-or-money formulas declared in the same paths: 5. Numeric formulas through a hop: 0.
3. The inspector hands the producer the host object's fields only. `git grep -n "inferFormulaReturnDeclaration(source, siblingDefs)" origin/main -- ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/ObjectFieldInspector.tsx` → line 1154.
4. The developer's "#37847 reads this export" constraint has lapsed: `gh api repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/issues/37847 --jq .state` → `closed`. It is not a cost of B any more.
5. PR #38108 is open, draft, head `b9bc5f06`: `gh api repos/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pulls/38108 --jq '[.state,.draft,.head.sha]'`.

## Options, real cost, workload

| | What is done | What the author sees | Workload |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | Nothing further; the limit stays in the producer header as PR #38108 writes it | After such an edit the field still draws a currency symbol until the author sets the result type to number in the inspector; stored values unaffected | 0 PRs |
| B | The producer takes related objects' field maps (or a reference-target member plus a resolver); the inspector loads each referenced object's fields before it asks | The currency mark is dropped on that edit, as it now is for same-object arithmetic | server + ui lanes, about 2 PRs (producer with a minor changeset; inspector). No precedent for widening the producer's inputs or for a hop-driven field load: `git log -S` is unusable here (shallow clone, 356 commits), so read from the PR list instead. Nearest landed sizes: PR #22733 introduced the producer, +715/−60, 29 files; PR #35774 wired the inspector to it, +475/−62, 10 files |

A and B differ by more than 3× in workload (0 against two PRs of the #35774 class); axis ① reads the same way, so the gap does not drive the letter.

Business meaning. A: the result type is the author's declaration, like a column format in a spreadsheet; the platform corrects it only when it is certain, and tells the truth about where its certainty ends. B: the platform follows the formula across objects to keep the label right, like a spell-checker that also opens the other document.

## Four axes

- Long-term soundness. End state in two years: a formula's result type is a declaration the author owns, and authoring help covers what can be proved from the object in hand. Salesforce and Airtable both model it that way: the formula's return type or format is chosen by the author and is never withdrawn by the platform when the expression changes, cross-object formulas included. A keeps one input (the host object's fields) and one stated limit. B adds a second input and a resolver to a published function, for one shape, and every multi-hop, polymorphic-reference and unpublished-draft case becomes a new edge the producer must define.
- Business pull. Nobody hits it today: 0 of 2 first-party currency formulas and 0 of 5 numeric ones read through a hop; all 6 hop formulas are text. The failure is a display label on an authoring edit, corrected in one click, and it only arises on a specific rewrite (money into hop quantity).
- AI-mistake resistance. Under A the wrong state is silent but narrow: an AI or human author who rewrites the expression and leaves `currency` declared gets a money face on a number; no door refuses it. B fixes it only inside Studio's inspector; an agent writing metadata files never passes through the inspector, so B does not close the silent case for AI-authored apps either. A loud fix would be a publish-time check, which is a new gate and not proposed.
- Startup focus. B is a declared, published surface with no consumer asking for it; once exported it is a permanent obligation. A declares nothing.

os-decision-facets
① Long-term soundness: A shrinks nothing and grows nothing; B grows the published producer contract (a second input or a resolver) for one shape. Reads A.
② Business pull: zero measured (0/2 currency formulas, 0/5 numeric formulas through a hop; 6 hop formulas, all text). Zero pull defaults to defer. Reads A.
③ AI-mistake resistance: both leave the file-authoring path silent; B is loud nowhere, it only corrects inside Studio. No difference that favours B. Reads A.
④ Startup focus: B adds a public surface and an inspector metadata read to maintain; A adds none. Reads A.
Prior rulings read: `label:needs-user-decision formula currency`, `inferFormulaReturn related object fields`, `formula currency relationship hop` → 0 rulings (1 / 12 issue hits, only #35815 on topic); ADR none; thread: #35815 (4 comments, no ruling)

## Recommendation

A. By ① alone: the declared-type model is the end state, and B's added input is contract growth for a shape nobody writes. B is not taken because it buys a display correction for zero measured users at the price of a permanent export.

Confidence gaps, stated and not used to change the letter: (a) the zero is measured over this repository's examples, platform objects and skills only; third-party and cloud tenant apps are outside the radius and were not read. (b) The symptom is read from code and the test pin, not driven in a browser. (c) B's size is the developer's estimate plus the two nearest landed PRs, not a precedent of the same change; the inspector already loads one related object's fields elsewhere (`useObjectFields(reference)`, `ObjectFieldInspector.tsx:2868`), so the async read is not new to the file, which may make B's inspector half smaller than stated.

只看①选 A;②③④ 是否翻转:否

## Execution after the answer

- A ⇒ the arm is closed as an accepted limit. PR #38108 lands as it stands (its header text already records the limit; no edit needed). This card is closed `not_planned` with the reason "zero measured pull; unproven keeps the declaration per the spec docblock"; the ruling id is quoted on #35815. Reopen only on a named external user.
- B ⇒ this card is retitled and retyped as a `Feature` card, Clause-②: yes (widening), minor changeset for `@objectstack/formula`, queued behind PR #38108 (`Blocked-by: #38108`, same file). Lane: `domain:server` for the producer PR, then `domain:ui` for the inspector PR. The producer PR must define multi-hop, polymorphic reference and missing-target behaviour (each stays `{}`), and removes the "Accepted limit" header section in the same PR.

## Related

#35815 (parent card, field-over-field arm and N3), PR #38108 (open draft, +162/−20), #35631 and PR #35774 (the currency verdict), PR #22733 (introduced `inferFormulaReturn`), #37847 (closed; no longer constrains the export).

Dedupe: `formula currency relationship hop` → 12 hits, `inferFormulaReturn related object fields` → 1 hit; only #35815 is on topic, and it is this card's parent.

Grade: area:data · Feature · p3 · reach: Studio authors who edit a currency formula into a lookup-hop quantity; display only · evidence read (0 first-party formulas of this shape)
